title: Technical flaws may inflate Australia's forest carbon credits
excerpt: AFPA has echoed serious concerns raised by Forestry Australia over the federal government's controversial new carbon credit method, warning it undermines the integrity and credibility of Australia's carbon market.
content_html:
AFPA has echoed serious concerns raised by Forestry Australia over the federal government's controversial new carbon credit method, warning it undermines the integrity and credibility of Australia's carbon market.

Forestry Australia has identified significant technical flaws in the new Improved Native Forest Management in Multiple-use Public Native Forests Method (INFM), with its forest carbon experts warning it could substantially overstate carbon abatement.

The latest analysis also shows the method could over-credit projects by between 40% and 100%, even before accounting for carbon leakage and harvested wood products.

AFPA Acting CEO Richard Hyett said the alarming independent research reinforced concerns the sustainable forest products industry had been raising for more than 18 months.

"As we have highlighted on several occasions, this method does not meet the Australian Carbon Credit Unit (ACCU) scheme's own requirements for integrity, transparency or additionality," Hyett said.

"The decision to register the method clearly prioritized politics over science and will damage public confidence in the integrity and transparency of the scheme."

Hyett said the method would generate carbon credits without delivering genuine additional emissions reductions and relied on science that had been challenged by independent experts and government scientists.

"We are very concerned the new method could flood the market with low-integrity ACCUs, undermining confidence in legitimate carbon projects and weakening investment in genuine climate action.

"Australia's carbon credit scheme is designed to encourage real carbon abatement and high-integrity environmental outcomes, and it's important the scheme remains focused on delivering genuine emissions reductions rather than being used to retrospectively fund policy decisions.

"Our carbon credit scheme is a critical part of Australia's framework to meet net-zero ambitions, and it's vital that its integrity is maintained to deliver genuine carbon abatement."

content_html_zh:
AFPA 回应了澳大利亚林业局对联邦政府颇具争议的新碳信用额方法提出的严重担忧，警告称该方法损害了澳大利亚碳市场的完整性和可信度。

澳大利亚林业局发现新的改进多用途公共原生林方法（INFM）中的原生林管理存在重大技术缺陷，其森林碳专家警告称，该方法可能大大夸大了碳减排量。

最新分析还表明，即使在考虑碳泄漏和采伐木材产品之前，该方法也可能对项目进行 40% 至 100% 的超额信贷。

AFPA 代理首席执行官理查德·海特 (Richard Hyett) 表示，令人震惊的独立研究加剧了 18 个多月以来对可持续林产品行业的担忧。

“正如我们多次强调的那样，这种方法不符合澳大利亚碳信用单位（ACCU）计划本身对完整性、透明度或额外性的要求，”海耶特说。

“注册该方法的决定显然将政治置于科学之上，并将损害公众对该计划完整性和透明度的信心。”

海耶特表示，该方法将产生碳信用额，但不会带来真正的额外减排，并且依赖于受到独立专家和政府科学家质疑的科学。

“我们非常担心新方法可能会让低诚信的 ACCU 充斥市场，从而削弱人们对合法碳项目的信心，并削弱对真正气候行动的投资。

“澳大利亚的碳信用计划旨在鼓励真正的碳减排和高度诚信的环境成果，重要的是该计划仍然专注于实现真正的减排，而不是用于追溯性地为政策决策提供资金。

“我们的碳信用计划是澳大利亚实现净零目标框架的重要组成部分，保持其完整性对于实现真正的碳减排至关重要。”
